newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: One hundred firms seek listing on Malaysia's OTC.
newsitem.headline: One hundred firms seek listing on Malaysia's OTC.

text.p: About 100 local and foreign companies have sought listing on the planned over-the-counter market for low capitalised, high-technology companies, Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar said on Thursday.

The national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying that Malaysian Exchange of Securities Dealing And Automated Quotation Bhd (Mesdaq) has received strong response since the framework for the OTC market was announced early this year.

"I have been told that the industry group, which has been given the task of setting up the market, has achieved much progress and details of this are expected to be made known shortly," he said at a two-day conference on Mesdaq.
The new exchange, expected to be launched early next year, is planned as a place for listing of small companies with high-growth potential but short or no track record, especially electronics firms.
Affifuddin said while future returns from Mesdaq-quoted companies might be greater, investors also face greater risks.
Mesdaq will operate in a full disclosure-based environment and will introduce higher standards of discipline and professionalism on all market intermediaries, he said.
Malaysia is modelling Mesdaq on the highly-successful electronic Nasdaq market in the United States.
Regulators have said that the over-the-counter market was to help with its planned Multimedia Super Corridor project, a proposed 15-by-50 km investment zone for high-technology firms.
Malaysia also wants to set up the complete gamut of financial options to become a regional financial hub competing with centres like Singapore and Hong Kong.
